filename: STRICTLY CONSTRAINED GENERATIVE MODELING VIA SPLIT AUGMENTED LANGEVIN SAMPLING.pdf
title: Strictly Constrained Generative Modeling via Split Augmented Langevin Sampling
testbed_rationale: The datasets generated and used are idealized 1D and 2D PDE benchmarks (Burgers, Darcy, Poisson, Navier-Stokes) designed for validating mathematical sampling and data assimilation algorithms rather than training Earth system model parameterizations.
pain_points: Generative models lack guarantees on physical plausibility and strict conservation laws (mass, energy).
Repeated projections in projected Langevin/diffusion dynamics cause chains to become trapped in local non-convex regions, hindering exploration.
Soft penalty guidance encourages constraint adherence on average but fails to enforce exact physical satisfaction.
Enforcing physical constraints in latent diffusion models typically requires backpropagating or inverting the decoder, which is computationally expensive and numerically ill-conditioned.
Unconstrained autoregressive or generative data assimilation models drift away from the true physical trajectory over time.
extraction_notes: The paper presents CASAL, a primal-dual split augmented Langevin sampling framework for strict constraint satisfaction in generative modeling. The publication year is noted as 2026 corresponding to the ICLR 2026 header.
